title: Subnet: local or remote?
hints: Compare both addresses using the local prefix.
Matching network portions mean local delivery.

variants.prompt: A host is 10.10.20.15/24 and sends to 10.10.20.200. Is the destination local or remote? Answer local or remote.
variants.explanation: Both addresses are in 10.10.20.0/24, so the host delivers directly after resolving the destination MAC.

title: ARP: choose the next hop
hints: First decide whether the destination is on the local subnet.
For remote traffic, ARP resolves the local gateway.

variants.prompt: Host 10.10.10.2/24 uses gateway 10.10.10.1 and sends to 10.200.10.8. Which IP does it ARP for?
variants.explanation: The server is remote, so the host resolves the MAC address of its local next hop, the default gateway.

title: Trunk VLAN preservation
hints: Compare allowed VLANs at both ends.
Adding differs from replacing an allowed list.

variants.prompt: A trunk currently allows VLANs 10 and 99, but students in VLAN 20 cannot cross it. What EOS command adds VLAN 20 without removing existing VLANs?
variants.explanation: The add form preserves VLANs 10 and 99 while allowing VLAN 20.

title: Route selection
hints: Prefer the longest matching prefix.
Only compare administrative distance after prefix length.

variants.prompt: Routes exist for 10.0.0.0/8 and 10.20.0.0/16. Which route matches destination 10.20.8.5? Answer the prefix.
variants.explanation: Both routes match, but /16 is the longest prefix and therefore wins.

title: OSPF neighbor evidence
hints: Verify adjacency before assuming routes should appear.
Use the command that lists OSPF neighbors.

variants.prompt: After configuring OSPF, which command directly verifies whether a neighbor adjacency exists?
variants.explanation: The neighbor command shows adjacency state; a configuration alone does not prove an adjacency formed.

title: ACL first-match behavior
hints: ACL entries are examined from top to bottom.
The first matching entry decides the result.

variants.prompt: An ACL permits IP any any before denying TCP host 10.1.1.10 any eq 22. Is SSH from 10.1.1.10 permitted or denied?
variants.explanation: The earlier permit ip any any matches first, so the later SSH deny is never reached.

title: EOS CLI mode workflow
hints: Start from privileged EXEC mode.
Global configuration is one command from privileged EXEC.

variants.prompt: From switch#, which command enters global configuration mode?
variants.explanation: configure terminal enters global configuration mode from privileged EXEC; the prompt becomes switch(config)#.

title: Running versus startup configuration
hints: A working change is not necessarily saved.
Compare active and saved configuration deliberately.

variants.prompt: A configuration works now but must survive a reboot. Which EOS command saves it?
variants.explanation: The running configuration is active now; copying it to startup-config preserves it across a reboot.

title: Interface evidence first
hints: Start with the lowest unproven dependency.
Use the concise interface state view before changing configuration.

variants.prompt: A VLAN user is offline and link state has not been proven. Which command gives a concise status view of all interfaces?
variants.explanation: show interfaces status is an efficient first check for administrative and link-state evidence before assuming a VLAN fault.

title: LACP compatibility
hints: LACP needs at least one side to initiate negotiation.
Do not mix static and negotiated aggregation.

variants.prompt: Two switches use LACP passive on both ends of a port-channel. Will the LACP bundle form? Answer yes or no.
variants.explanation: Passive/passive provides no initiator, so LACP negotiation does not form the bundle. Active/passive or active/active can form it.

title: MLAG role distinction
hints: One port-channel connects the two peers.
Another can connect a dual-attached downstream device.

variants.prompt: In an MLAG design, what connects the two MLAG peer switches: the peer link or the downstream MLAG port-channel?
variants.explanation: The peer link connects the two peers. A downstream MLAG port-channel connects a dual-attached device to the peer pair.

title: Static default route
hints: A default route matches destinations without a more specific route.
Use the IPv4 prefix 0.0.0.0/0.

variants.prompt: Configure an IPv4 default route through next hop 192.0.2.1. Enter the EOS command.
variants.explanation: A static default route uses 0.0.0.0/0 and the reachable next-hop address.

title: OSPF troubleshooting order
hints: Do not assume routes are the first thing to check.
Adjacency is a prerequisite to learning routes dynamically.

variants.prompt: OSPF routes are missing after configuration. Which should be verified first: neighbor adjacency or the OSPF route table?
variants.explanation: An OSPF adjacency is a prerequisite for learning routes. Prove the neighbor state before interpreting absent OSPF routes.
